subject: Trading
title: Carl Icahn: The Corporate Raider
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Carl Icahn: The Corporate Raider.

hook.text: Carl Icahn buys stakes in companies he thinks are badly managed—then fights to change them or force a sale.

buildup.text: Known as a corporate raider, Icahn pressures boards to unlock value—spinoffs, buybacks, management changes.

discovery.text: His targets are companies with cheap shares and bad leadership. He profits when better management boosts value.

twist.text: The 'Icahn Lift'—stocks often jump just on news that he's taken a position, because markets expect activist change.

climax.text: Icahn shows that buying undervalued companies isn't enough—sometimes you need to fix them yourself to unlock value.

punchline.text: He doesn't wait for value to surface. He forces it.

quiz.question: What is the 'Icahn Lift'?
options: The stock price jump that occurs when Icahn takes an activist position
